Directions: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Professionalism is probably the _____ (A) theoretical of the types of soft skills, and certainly the most dependent on context. What professionalism ______ (B) in one organization can be very different from what it means in another. In general, what most employers mean when they say they are _______ (C) for professionalism is someone who understands how they as an individual affect the ______ (D) as a whole. That can mean anything from personal performance related to broad standards, or how one's ______ (E) impacts the health of the team.

Select the appropriate word to fill blank B.
questions.solution_en:
The blank requires a verb that indicates the connection related to professionalism and organization. 'Explains' (give a reason so as to justify or excuse (an action or event)) and 'ignored' (refuse to take notice of or acknowledge; disregard intentionally) are contextually irrelevant words as 'professionalism' cannot do these two actions in the context of an organization, so they are negated. 'Avoiding' is in a continuous form that does not have an auxiliary verb to support it, so it is also negated. 'Means' (intend to convey or refer to (a particular thing); signify) is the most appropriate word that indicates the role of professionalism in the given context of the sentence.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

Note:

Auxiliary verb: A verb that gives grammatical information that is not given by the main verb of a sentence. It supports the main verb. Auxiliary verbs help to form the various tenses, moods, and voices of other verbs. The principal ones are be, do, and have. Example: She will sing a song tomorrow. Here, 'will' is the auxiliary verb that supports the main verb 'sing'.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate article(s) to fill in the blanks.

Every ____ year, many people all over ____ world need new organs to continue enjoying their lives.
questions.solution_en:
The phrase "every year" does not require an article in between because "every" itself conveys a sense of regularity and encompasses all years in a recurring manner. Adding "a" or "an" would be incorrect, as "every" already provides the necessary grammatical structure. So, no article is required in the first blank.

The definite article "the" should be used in the second blank because "world" is unique and universally understood as a specific entity. There is only one world being referred to here, so "the" is appropriate.

The complete sentence is: Every year, many people all over the world need new organs to continue enjoying their lives.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

Note: Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun or plural noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun or singular noun.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The new sunshades have protected our windows during the rainy season.
options_en: Our windows are being protected by the new window during the rainy season.
Our windows are being protected by the new sunshades during the rainy season.
Our sunshades have been protected by the windows during the rainy season.
Our windows have been protected by the new during the rainy season.
questions.solution_en:
To convert the active voice sentence to passive voice:

The object ("our windows") becomes the subject.

The verb "have protected" (present perfect) becomes "have been protected" (passive form: have/has + been + past participle).

The subject ("the new sunshades") becomes the agent, introduced by the preposition "by."

The correct option that maintains the tense (present perfect) and uses "sunshades" correctly is option (4), "Our windows have been protected by the new sunshades during the rainy season."

(a) Our windows are being protected by the new window: Incorrect tense (present continuous "are being protected" vs. present perfect). Also, "window" is incorrect; the original subject is "sunshades."

(b) Our windows are being protected by the new sunshades: Incorrect tense (present continuous instead of present perfect).

(c) Our sunshades have been protected by the new windows: Correct tense but wrong subject ("windows" instead of "sunshades").

Hence, the correct answer is option (3).

questions.q_en:
Directions [Set of 4 Questions]: Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.

The introduction of African cheetahs to India was planned without considering their spatial ecology, according to researchers who warn that the released animals may come into conflict with people in the neighbouring villages. Spatial ecology addresses the fundamental effects of space on the movement of individual species and on the stability of multispecies communities. A total of 20 cheetahs from Namibia and South Africa were introduced to Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh last year to establish a free-ranging population - for the first time since their extinction in India 70 years ago. Scientists of the Cheetah Research Project of Leibniz-IZW in Namibia argue that in southern Africa, cheetahs live in a stable socio-spatial system with widely spread territories and densities of less than one individual per 100 square kilometres (km²). The plan for cheetahs in Kuno National Park assumes that the high prey density will sustain high cheetah densities, even though there is no evidence for that, they said. In a letter published in the journal Conservation Science and Practice on Thursday, researchers noted that as Kuno National Park is small, it is likely that the released animals will move far beyond the park's boundaries and cause conflicts with neighbouring villages.

According to a calculation of the local prey density, it was calculated that 21 adult cheetahs could be sustained by the prey base in Kuno National Park - equivalent to a density of about three individuals per 100 km². Based on their research results from a long-term study of the spatial behaviour of cheetahs in Namibia, as well as comparable work in East Africa, scientists from the Leibniz Institute for Zoo and Leibniz-IZW warn against overestimating the carrying capacity of the area. The carrying capacity is usually between 0.2 and 1 adult per 100 km² for cheetahs under natural conditions. This is true not only for Namibia but also for the ecologically very different conditions in the Serengeti ecosystem in East Africa which has a much higher density of prey, they said. The team formulated predictions about the spatial behaviour of cheetahs in their new habitat, identifying controversial issues and hidden core assumptions of the reintroduction plan. These assumptions ignore important aspects of the cheetah socio-spatial system.

Why did the authorities think Cheetahs could sustain themselves in the small boundaries of Kuno National Park?
options_en: The meagreness of the prey could help the sustainability of cheetahs.
The availability of prey could sustain more cheetahs in a limited space.
High number of cheetahs could control the number of prey.
A large number of prey and food sources can only be reduced with a high number of cheetahs.
questions.solution_en:
The first paragraph states that "The plan for cheetahs in Kuno National Park assumes that the high prey density will sustain high cheetah densities, even though there is no evidence for that, they said." According to this, the authorities thought that a large number of prey could help sustain a high density of cheetahs.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank(s).

_____ bullet missed his heart by ____ couple of centimetres.
questions.solution_en:
The most appropriate option to fill in the blanks is (d). The article "the" is used before "bullet" to refer to a specific bullet, the one being discussed in the context of narrowly missing the heart. Using "a" before "bullet" implies any bullet, which doesn't fit the context that refers to a specific bullet that narrowly missed the heart. 'An' is the indefinite article used before words that begin with a vowel sound. However, "bullet" starts with a consonant sound. So, "an" is not appropriate here.

The article "a" is used before "couple" to indicate any indefinite or unspecified couple of centimetres. Using "the" before "couple" suggests a specific or previously mentioned couple of centimetres, which does not align with the intended meaning of an unspecified distance. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

The referee declared that the participant who will score the highest points in the tally will take away the cash prize of 50 lakh.
options_en: who can score the highest point
who could score the highest point
who settles scores the highest point
questions.solution_en:
The sentence requires the present tense "scores" for a general rule about the competition, and "points" should remain plural for consistency.

Who can score the highest point: "Can" implies possibility, not certainty, and "point" is singular, incorrect for a tally.

Who could score the highest point: Past tense "could" and singular "point" are incorrect.

Who settles scores the highest point: Illogical phrasing and singular "point."

The correct sentence: The referee declared that the participant who scores the highest points in the tally will take away the cash prize of 50 lakh.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

questions.q_en: Select the correct sentence in passive voice from the following options.
options_en: His friends invited themselves to the surprise birthday party.
I said to him, "I will invite all your friends to the surprise birthday party".
I invited his friends to the surprise birthday party.
His friends were invited to the surprise birthday party by me.
questions.solution_en:
(a) - This sentence is in active voice. The subject (friends) performed the action (invited themselves).

(b) - This sentence is in active voice. The subject (I) will perform the action (will invite).

(c) - This sentence is in active voice. The subject (I) performed the action (invited).

(d) - This sentence is in passive voice. The focus is on the friends (the receiver of the action), and the doer of the action (me) is mentioned with the preposition "by." This option fits the passive voice construction: Object + a form of "to be" + past participle (invited) + by + the doer of the action (optional).

Therefore, option (d) is the correct answer in passive voice.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

The manager said that Anand had cleared the dues.
options_en: The manager said, "Anand has been clearing the dues."
The manager said, "Anand cleared the dues."
The manager said, "Anand is clearing the dues."
The manager said, "Anand will have cleared the dues."
questions.solution_en:
The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Past Simple Tense.

Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 + Object) will be converted into Past Simple (Subject + V2 + Object).

For example:

He said that Arya had sent him a book. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "Arya sent me a book" (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

Indirect SpeechDirect Speech
Said thatsaid
had clearedcleared

From the given options, the sentence that follows the above mentioned conditions for Direct speech is option (b) "The manager said, "Anand cleared the dues.""

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

NOTE:

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).
